Your question refers to **CIB** (Commercial International Bank), but every piece of evidence supplied in this file relates to **COMI** (Commodity & Industrial Investment Company). I can only analyse the COMI data that was provided; I have no CIB evidence to work from. If you intended COMI, the analysis below applies. If you truly need CIB, that evidence must be supplied separately.

---

## COMI – Net Profit & Growth (FY2025 vs FY2024)

### Net profit (income statement)

| Period | Value (as printed) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Dec 31, 2025 | 82,258,815 EGP 000s → **82,258,815,000 EGP** | **AMBIGUOUS** – digits partially hidden by a fold in the scanned page [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-33] |
| Dec 31, 2024 | 55,256,732 EGP 000s → **55,256,732,000 EGP** | Verified [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-34] |

Because the 2025 net-profit figure is flagged **AMBIGUOUS**, I **cannot** compute a reliable year-on-year net-profit growth rate from the income statement. Any percentage derived from 82,258,815 would be unreliable.

### Basic EPS (verified proxy)

| Period | EPS (EGP) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Dec 31, 2025 | 18.25 | Verified [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-39] |
| Dec 31, 2024 | 14.72 | Verified [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-40] |

EPS growth = (18.25 − 14.72) / 14.72 = **≈ 24.0 %**

> Caveat: EPS growth equals net-profit growth only if the weighted-average share count is unchanged. No share-count data is in the evidence, so this is a proxy, not a confirmed net-profit growth figure.

### Against your 30 % threshold

- The **verified** EPS-based growth of ~24 % is **below** your 30 % trigger.
- The **ambiguous** 2025 net-profit figure, if read at face value (82,258,815 vs 55,256,732), would imply ≈ 48.9 % growth – well above 30 %. However, because that figure is **AMBIGUOUS** (fold in the scan), I **cannot** treat it as confirmed and therefore **cannot** validate that the 30 % threshold is met.

---

## Data-Quality & Risk Notes

1. **Scan defect:** The 2025 net-profit cell is partially obscured [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-33]. Until a clean copy or the auditor's report confirms the digit, the figure should be treated as unverified.
2. **Single-period evidence:** Only FY2025 and FY2024 are available; no multi-year trend, segment split, or cash-flow statement is provided, limiting the growth and balance-sheet assessment.
3. **No balance-sheet or cash-flow data** was supplied, so leverage, liquidity, and working-capital risk cannot be evaluated from this evidence set.
4. **Unit check:** All income-statement figures are in EGP thousands; EPS is in EGP per share. Conversions above reflect that.

---

## Bottom Line for Your Decision

- I **cannot confirm** that COMI's net profit grew by more than 30 % in FY2025 because the 2025 figure is AMBIGUOUS.
- The only **verified** growth signal (basic EPS) points to roughly **24 %**, which would **not** meet your 30 % add-on trigger.
- Before acting on the 30 % rule, you would need a clean, verified copy of the FY2025 net-profit line (or the audited annual report) to resolve the ambiguity.

*No buy/sell/hold recommendation is made here; that is the decision agent's role.*

## Note on the Question

The evidence supplied in this report is for **COMI** (the only holding in the portfolio), not for **CIB**. I have no CIB figures to work from, so I cannot confirm or deny a >30 % net-profit growth for CIB. In addition, my remit here is investor-suitability, not company-fundamental analysis, so I will not compute a growth rate from the COMI numbers that are printed.

If you intended to ask about **COMI**, the two net-profit figures are visible in the evidence (Dec 2025: 82,258,815 EGP-thousands; Dec 2024: 55,256,732 EGP-thousands), but I will leave the arithmetic to the research team.

---

## Suitability Snapshot

| Dimension | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Goal** | Grow savings |
| **Horizon** | 4 years – medium term; enough time to ride out a single market cycle, but not long enough to ignore drawdowns |
| **Liquidity needs** | Low – a separate emergency fund is maintained, so portfolio cash is not earmarked for short-term bills |
| **Willingness to accept losses** | Medium – comfortable with moderate volatility, but not a "set-and-forget" high-beta investor |
| **Capacity to absorb losses** | Medium – a large drawdown would be felt but not catastrophic |

### Current concentration

| Item | Value (EGP) | Share of total |
|---|---|---|
| COMI – 100 sh × 128.00 | 12,800 | ≈ 39 % |
| Cash | 20,000 | ≈ 61 % |
| **Total** | **32,800** | 100 % |

The portfolio is **single-stock concentrated** on the equity side (100 % of the invested portion is COMI), but the large cash buffer keeps overall equity exposure modest.

### What the portfolio allows

- **Cash that is free to deploy:** the full **20,000 EGP** (emergency fund is held separately, so none of this cash is restricted).
- **Equity that can be sold:** all **100 COMI shares** (≈ 12,800 EGP at the cutoff price) if a rebalance or exit is desired.
- **No other holdings, no pledged assets, no near-term known outflows** are noted.

### Fit observations (no action recommended)

- A 4-year horizon with medium loss tolerance/capacity is broadly consistent with a **mixed allocation** (e.g., a blend of equities and fixed-income or money-market instruments) rather than an all-equity or all-cash posture.
- The current 61 % cash / 39 % single-stock split sits at the conservative end; the investor has room to shift some of the 20,000 EGP cash into additional instruments if the research team identifies suitable opportunities, without breaching the medium-loss tolerance.
- Because the only equity is a single name, any new equity commitment would either **add to COMI concentration** (raising single-stock risk) or **diversify** (reducing it). The suitability constraint is the medium loss capacity: a further large single-stock position would push concentration risk beyond what "medium" comfortably supports.
- The investor's stated trigger ("I will add if it grew by more than 30 %") is a **fundamental-growth condition** that belongs to the research/valuation team, not to the suitability assessment. From a suitability standpoint, the 20,000 EGP cash is available to act on such a trigger, subject to the concentration and loss-tolerance limits above.

*I have not analysed COMI's (or CIB's) financials and I am not recommending a buy, sell, or hold.*
